profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page, this building, marketed as SV1 and mapped here as the San Jose Colocation Center, is located at 55 S. Market St., San Jose, CA 95113. CoreSite publishes more than 320,000 square feet for this building, a figure consistent across the facility page, the Silicon Valley regional overview, and the operator's own spec sheet. No MW capacity or opening year is stated. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance for its facilities generally.

CoreSite's Silicon Valley presence spans nine named buildings across San Jose, Santa Clara, and Milpitas, which the operator's regional overview page describes as totaling more than 1.4 million square feet campus-wide, with the Santa Clara sub-campus (SV3 through SV9) separately described in a CoreSite construction-approval release as exceeding 775,000 square feet on its own. CoreSite is a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation (NYSE: AMT), which completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021; Stonepeak Partners LP separately acquired roughly 29% of American Tower's US data center business in July 2022, later increased to about 36%. CoreSite's own site describes a total portfolio of 30 data centers across 11 US markets totaling more than 4.8 million square feet, with more than 44,000 customer interconnections and 500-plus connected network providers.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance; the company also budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026, funding continued build-out across CoreSite's 11-market US portfolio, of which Silicon Valley remains among the largest by building count and total square footage.

profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite cluster spans Los Angeles, San Jose, Santa Clara, and Santa Clara County, California, the company founding home turf. Wikipedia coverage states CoreSite was established in 2001 as CRG West, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. In May 2007 the company acquired Santa Clara land for a planned 50 megawatt data center as part of a wider expansion that also added Boston and Chicago properties. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. As of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with Los Angeles and San Francisco/San Jose/Santa Clara both listed among its key markets. American Tower completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. No building specific address or individual MW figures for these particular registry rows were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite's San Jose facility occupies 320,000 square feet in downtown San Jose at 55 South Market Street. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity or opening year for this building. The certifications listed—SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and NIST 800-53—qualify the campus to host regulated workloads across financial services, healthcare, and government sectors.

This facility is one of nine CoreSite buildings across the Silicon Valley region, which together total more than 1.4 million square feet. CoreSite operates 30 data centers across 11 US markets with more than 4.8 million square feet total, making Silicon Valley one of its largest regional clusters by building count and square footage. American Tower, which acquired CoreSite in late 2021, reported record leasing at the operator in 2026 and budgeted $695 million for data center development across the CoreSite portfolio that year.

Without published capacity, this San Jose facility cannot be ranked against peers. California has 103 mapped data center facilities, but only 11 publish megawatt figures totaling 365 MW. CoreSite's published capacity statewide ranks 12th by our records. Whether this 320,000-square-foot building holds material AI load depends entirely on its power supply and internal density, neither of which is public.
